note: 2022 MCM A, team 2210307. 21 figure rows (20 numbered plus one uncaptioned leaflet radar) and 14 measured tables, over 50 measured regions, with 15 excluded. Three tables are emitted by the layout pass as several stacked bands because their cells wrap (Table 1 on p6, Table 2 on p8, Table 3 on p13); the extra bands are excluded as fragments of the recorded row. Four tables (5 and 8, 6 and 9) are near-duplicates of each other by design - one pair per course - and their captions repeat word for word. The paper has one table with no caption and no measured region at all: the notations list under section 3 on p4, which the crop audit reads as an unruled three-column grid; it is declared here instead of being recorded. The last two pages are a leaflet, not body text: p24 is decoration and banner labels (all four regions excluded), p25 carries the only uncaptioned chart in the paper. Figures 3 and 4 of the earlier 2022 papers have no analogue here - every numbered figure in this paper is measured.
rules: Every table caption sits above its grid and every figure caption below its graphic, with no exception in 14 tables and 21 figures [caption.position].
The family mix is curve-heavy and map-heavy: line 12, map-or-plan-view 3, flowchart-or-schematic 3, table-grid 14, scatter 1, surface-or-3D 1, composite-panel 1 [geometry.family].

Radar wheels are recorded as line: Figure 10's three wheels in one row and the leaflet's hexagon carry no scale ticks, so they are polygons on radial axes rather than a family of their own [geometry.family] [geometry.shared_axes].

Three-dimensional rendering appears exactly once, as Figure 7's perspective terrain ribbon with a mesh floor; the eleven result figures of section 6 are all flat, and the only other depth cue in the paper is a colour-banded elevation profile [geometry.three_d].

Every multi-variable time series in section 6 stacks three quantities on one frame with three y-scales (power left, speed right, elevation far right) and a legend under the frame, rather than using stacked panels [geometry.panel_layout].

Section 6 repeats one figure-and-two-table block three times, once per course: a course map, an elevation profile, a course-information table and an environmental table. Captions are recycled verbatim across the blocks - 'Course elevation proﬁle.' at Figures 12, 16 and 19, 'Diagram of power, speed, elevation and distance.' at Figures 13, 17 and 20, 'Course information' at Tables 5, 8 and 11, 'Course environmental factors' at Tables 6, 9 and 12 [caption.verbatim] [geometry.family].

Course-information and environmental tables are one-row tables with the unit written inside each cell ('15.7 C', '0.96 atm', '7.5m/s'), while the two calculation-result tables (7 and 10) put the unit in the header ('Length km', 'Output power W') [table.units_in_header].

The three grid tables of section 4-5 are zebra-striped in pale violet; none of the eleven course tables is striped, and none of the fourteen uses interior vertical rules [table.zebra] [table.rule_style].

The citing spelling is the capitalised full word 'Figure N' or 'Table N' with no abbreviation, and 27 of the 35 rows are never cited by a numbered sentence at all - they are reached only through their own caption or through a deictic 'as follows' [mention.style] [mention.lead_pattern].

Captions are noun phrases with no finite verb on every row and every numbered caption is a single sentence, 4 to 17 words; the long ones stretch the explanation with comma clauses inside the title rather than adding a second sentence (Figure 3, 17 words, defines t and P in a parenthetical) [caption.voice] [caption.sentences] [caption.words].

Numbering is not stable: the body calls Table 5 'Table 7' two lines above the caption, Tables 2 and 3 carry the same caption word for word although their contents differ, and the leaflet's radar has no number at all [mention.count] [caption.numbering].
